title: Crystal electric field excitations and an effective-spin-$1/2$ ground doublet in the hyperkagome magnet Yb$_3$Sc$_2$Ga$_3$O$_{12}$
authors: Tingjun Zhang, Zehao Wang, Douglas L. Abernathy, Rong-Zhu Lin, Steven J. Gomez Alvarado, Chien-Lung Huang, Pengcheng Dai
abstract: We use inelastic neutron scattering (INS) to determine the crystal electric field (CEF) excitations of Yb$^{3+}$ in the rare-earth hyperkagome magnet Yb$_3$Sc$_2$Ga$_3$O$_{12}$. Three nearly dispersionless magnetic excitations are observed near 58, 68, and 74~meV, corresponding to transitions from the ground-state Kramers doublet to the three excited doublets of the $J=7/2$ multiplet. A Stevens-operator analysis constrained by the local $222$ ($D_2$) symmetry reproduces the excitation energies and spectral weights and yields an Ising-type ground-state $g$ tensor. The first excited doublet lies approximately 58~meV above the ground state, establishing a well-isolated effective $J_{\mathrm{eff}}=1/2$ degree of freedom over the low-temperature regime relevant to collective magnetism. Notably, the directly measured CEF spectrum substantially revises the level scheme previously inferred from bulk measurements, while preserving the essential low-energy pseudospin description. Two independent fitting protocols give consistent excitation energies, ground-doublet wave functions, and $g$ tensors, despite the nonuniqueness of the individual CEF parameters. The resulting single-ion model also reproduces the characteristic susceptibility, magnetization, and field evolution of the Schottky anomaly in specific heat. These results establish the microscopic single-ion basis needed to construct an effective exchange Hamiltonian and to interpret future measurements of low-energy collective excitations in Yb$_3$Sc$_2$Ga$_3$O$_{12}$.
summary: This work uses inelastic neutron scattering to map the crystal electric field excitations of Yb3+ in the hyperkagome magnet Yb3Sc2Ga3O12. By fitting the observed spectrum, the authors establish a microscopic single-ion model that successfully reproduces bulk magnetic properties. This model isolates an effective spin-1/2 ground state, providing the necessary foundation to study low-energy collective quantum magnetism.
main_problem: To determine the crystal electric field (CEF) excitations and establish the effective low-energy magnetic description in the hyperkagome magnet Yb3Sc2Ga3O12.
main_result: INS measurements confirm three CEF excitations, and the analysis establishes the low-energy physics is governed by a well-isolated effective J_eff=1/2 Kramers doublet.
method: The study combines inelastic neutron scattering (INS) experiments with detailed single-ion modeling using Stevens-operator analysis.
model_or_system: The system is the rare-earth hyperkagome magnet Yb3Sc2Ga3O12, focusing on the J=7/2 multiplet of the Yb3+ ion. The CEF Hamiltonian is analyzed using local D2h symmetry constraints.
key_observables: Three nearly dispersionless magnetic excitations observed near 58, 68, and 74 meV; the effective g tensor components (e.g., g_z > g_x > g_y).
important_parameters: The low-energy physics is described by an effective J_eff=1/2 degree of freedom; the characteristic energy separation of the first excited doublet (~58 meV).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the low-energy behavior is dominated by an effective spin-1/2 doublet, despite the non-uniqueness of individual CEF parameters.
figures_summary: Figures show the crystal structure, INS data mapping the three CEF excitations, and comparisons of calculated single-ion properties (specific heat, susceptibility, magnetization) against experimental data.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by using INS to measure the full CEF spectrum, fitting this spectrum to determine CEF parameters, and finally using the resulting single-ion model to predict and reproduce bulk magnetic observables like specific heat and magnetization.
why_interesting: The rigorous determination of the single-ion basis (CEF parameters and effective g-tensor) is crucial for constructing an accurate effective exchange Hamiltonian, which is the starting point for understanding collective quantum magnetism in frustrated lattices.
